title: MAECI Italian Government Scholarship
degree: Bachelor's, Master's, PhD, Research, Language courses
official_source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI), Government of Italy
program_type: Government scholarship of the Italian Republic (legal basis Law 288/55)
duration: 9 months from 1 November 2026 to 31 July 2027 for the main grant categories; 3-month grants run from 1 January 2027 and must end by 30 September 2027
description: The Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation awards scholarships to foreign students and Italian citizens resident abroad (IRE) under Italian law 288/55, to foster cultural, scientific and technological cooperation and to promote Italian language and culture. Scholarships are available only for academic courses taught on Italian territory, and the call sets out separate categories for degree study, research grants and shorter language or training courses. title: Pearson International Scholarship (University of Toronto)
duration: Four years of full-time undergraduate study
description: The Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship is the University of Toronto's most prestigious award for international students and one of the largest scholarship programmes for international students in Canada. It covers tuition, books, incidental fees and full residence support for four years and is tenable only at the University of Toronto for first-entry undergraduate programmes. Around 37 scholars are named each year from a pool representing 188 countries, with more than CAD 12 million of funding in 2024. title: ARES Scholarships (Belgium)
program_type: International training scholarship (specialised bachelor's, specialised master's or continuing education)
duration: One academic year (12 months maximum) for specialised bachelor's and specialised master's degrees; 6 months maximum for continuing education
description: As part of its 2027-2032 five-year programme, ARES offers international training scholarships enabling permanent residents of partner countries to pursue a specialised bachelor's degree, a specialised master's degree or a continuing education course at an institution of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation in Belgium, while receiving a scholarship covering travel, subsistence, insurance and (for degrees) tuition.

title: AECID Spanish Government Scholarship
official_source: Agencia Española de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (AECID)
program_type: Government scholarship programme family (umbrella of sub-programmes)
duration: Varies by sub-programme: Roma residencies are four to nine months, always consecutive and within 1 October 2026 to 30 June 2027; Programa AFRICA-MED Master funds an official in-person Spanish master's of up to 60 ECTS; the Programa COE award runs from September 2026 to June 2027; Programa COOPERACION and CULT run over published destinations listed in ANEXO I and ANEXO II.
description: The MAEC-AECID programme family (Becas Cooperación Española) is run by the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) and funds training for Spanish citizens and for citizens of Spanish-cooperation partner countries, both in Spain and abroad. The official page groups the live 2026/2027 calls into four blocks: scholarships for young Spaniards, readerships (Lectorados) for Spaniards teaching Spanish abroad, scholarships for citizens of Latin America, Africa and Asia, and artistic or research residencies at the Real Academia de España en Roma. title: Australia Awards Fellowships
official_source: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), Australian Government
duration: 2 to 52 weeks per Fellowship. The Fellowship commences in Australia and is followed by in-partner country activities focused on implementation and exchange of expertise. The duration of the in-partner country activities must not exceed the duration of the activities in Australia. The mandatory compliance criteria add that at least two weeks must be delivered in Australia and that the total cannot exceed 52 weeks, counting in-Australia, online and in-partner country activity together.
description: Australia Awards Fellowships is a DFAT competitive grants programme in which an Australian organisation - never an individual - applies for funding to host a Fellow nominated by an overseas counterpart organisation in an eligible developing country. The grant is up to $34,500 per Fellow for a single Fellowship of 2 to 52 weeks, and the Australian Host Organisation must add a mandatory cash and/or in-kind co-contribution; DFAT publishes no tuition component, no living-cost rate and no separate airfare figure. title: Australia Awards Mekong-Australia Partnership (MAP) Scholarships
official_source: Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), Australian Government
duration: The minimum period necessary for the individual to complete the academic program specified by the Australian higher education institution, including any preparatory training
description: The Mekong-Australia Partnership (MAP) is a five-year commitment announced at the ASEAN-Australia Special Summit in March 2024, with a second phase of $222.5 million for 2024-2029 that includes additional Master's scholarships per year. MAP-funded scholarships let citizens of Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar undertake a Master's by research or coursework at an Australian tertiary institution, with benefits identical to Australia Awards plus exclusive access to the Mekong-Leaders Network.

title: Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP)
degree: Research Doctorate, Research Master's (Higher Degree by Research)
duration: Research doctorate: a minimum of 3 years and up to a maximum of 4 years at the discretion of the higher education provider for a full-time student load, and a minimum of 6 years up to a maximum of 8 years for a part-time student load. Research masters: up to 2 years full-time and up to 4 years part-time. A student's period of support is not increased for periods of paid recreation leave or personal leave approved by the provider; it is increased by the length of any approved RTP suspension, or any additional approved paid personal leave, paid parental leave, paid partner leave, or paid family and domestic violence leave.
description: The Research Training Program is Australian Government funding that flows to eligible universities as block grants, which those universities then use to offer scholarships to students doing a research doctorate or research masters. A scholarship may comprise one or more of three published components - a tuition fees offset, a stipend for general living costs, and allowances for the ancillary costs of a higher degree by research - and it is the university, not the Department, that decides the mix, applies, selects and sets the deadline. Stipend rates are indexed annually and published as a base
